{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4ee89a5656952dc360de261a4fabebd9c4d5edd328c75385741fd1dd59de3e58","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:94","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle Equipment, Safety Inspection and Maintenance","heading":"C2 — KG hints for Vehicle Equipment, Safety Inspection and Maintenance","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — KG hints for Vehicle Equipment, Safety Inspection and Maintenance

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A01
Ordinary vehicles are inspected once a year, while ambulances are inspected every six months and a newly sold vehicle is exempt until two years after its initial inspection [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint inspection; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec03-F05 and sec03-F06.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A03
A child under four needs a child restraint, while a child under eight needs a booster seat only when the child is under four feet tall and under forty pounds [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint occupant-protection; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec03-F21 and sec03-F20.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A03
Two inches of steering free play is the limit with power steering, while three inches is the limit without it [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint steering; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec03-F23 and sec03-F24.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A01
A red light to the front and a blue light visible outside are both reserved for authorized emergency vehicles, just as bells, exhaust whistles and sirens are [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint illegal-equipment; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec03-F02 and sec03-F03.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A02
The ordinary brake test is done at four to eight miles per hour, while antilock brakes usually need more than ten miles per hour to activate [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint brakes; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec03-F11 and sec03-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Air bags protect only in the first impact and then deflate, while safety belts protect through every impact of a crash [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint occupant-protection; prereq_hint sec03-R02; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec03-F22 and sec03-F20.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A03
Tire pressure is checked at least monthly against the door jamb label, while tread is replaced below one sixteenth of an inch as shown by the penny test [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint tires; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec03-F26 and sec03-F27.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A02
When turn indicators stop working, communicate turns with hand signals until repairs are made [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint lamps-and-signals; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec03-F14 and sec03-F13.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A01
The insurance identification card is needed to pass the inspection, while the inspection certificate is the document that must then remain in the vehicle [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint inspection; prereq_hint sec03-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec03-F08 and sec03-F09.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A02
A replacement muffler may not be louder than the original equipment muffler, while a muffler cut-out or by-pass is prohibited outright [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint illegal-equipment; prereq_hint sec03-R04; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec03-F16 and sec03-F04.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0019]
